reason: Brooks's page-194 theorem applies to a network or linear graph, explicitly excludes loops, and defines an n-simplex using one line joining each pair, but it does not explicitly forbid multiple lines joining a pair. Lean SimpleGraph cannot represent parallel lines. The candidate SimpleGraph envelope is therefore a potentially restricted corollary, not an exact source-domain target, until an admitted source decision and checked model transport exist. Collapsing parallel lines is a plausible reduction: it preserves components and proper colorings and weakly decreases degrees; if the collapsed graph contained a K_(n+1) component, the source degree bound would force the original component to have exactly those lines and no parallel extras, contradicting the n-simplex exclusion. That argument remains unformalized and independently unreviewed. Complete source admission, the proof/premise and correction audit, and predecessor master acceptance are also open.
